import html # Template for rendering a user profile. PROFILE_FORMAT = """

{name}

{bio}

{status_msg}
""" def show_user_profile(name: str, bio: str, status_msg: str) -> str: """ Return a sanitized HTML snippet containing the user's profile. Parameters ---------- name : str The user's name. bio : str A potentially multi‑sentence biography. May contain user supplied text. status_msg : str Short one‑liner status message from the user. Returns ------- str A safe, sanitized HTML string ready for embedding in a page. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not of type `str`. """ # Validate input types. if not isinstance(name, str): raise TypeError("name must be a string") if not isinstance(bio, str): raise TypeError("bio must be a string") if not isinstance(status_msg, str): raise TypeError("status_msg must be a string") # Escape user supplied data to avoid XSS. safe_name = html.escape(name, quote=True) safe_bio = html.escape(bio, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") safe_status = html.escape(status_msg, quote=True) # Format the profile using the template. return PROFILE_FORMAT.format( name=safe_name, bio=safe_bio, status_msg=safe_status )
